parsed.corrected_rationale: The comment expresses agreement and offers a personal theoretical observation: "utilizing the entire training text data could mitigate this issue." This is framed as the reviewer's own opinion about why semantic loss may fail, not as a direct request for the authors to modify their paper. At most, an action can be implicitly inferred (that the authors might consider using more/full training data), but the comment does not explicitly state a modification the authors should apply, and even the inferred action is vague — it gives no detail on how to incorporate full training text into fine-tuning or what specific changes to make. The claim that "the authors know they should use more data" overreads the text, since the statement is prefaced by "Theoretically" and is presented as speculation rather than a concrete suggestion. Thus the comment contains at best an implicit, vague action without guidance on implementation, which corresponds to the lower end of the rubric rather than an explicitly stated action.
